title: Earlier recordings with the Quality Serenaders and Armstrong
summary: His first recordings were for Victor with Paul Howard's band, then Mosby and Armstrong in Los Angeles in 1930.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Oh, the first time I ever recorded was in California, on Victor, with the Quality Seranaders, Paul Howard's Quality Seranaders. And then I recorded some with the other fellow, Mosby's. And then we recorded on our own name, Quality Seranaders. Paul -- I mean Lawrence, Charlie Lawrence was the orchestrator and arranger. You just made numbers and numbers everywhere.
Do you remember what you recorded --
No, no. I don't have any, so I don't remember any.
But when you started recording, do you know what year was it? That same year, was it '32, or was it before that?
I recorded, oh first I recorded -- one
of the first I recorded with was Louie Armstrong. That's one recorded, "In the Market for You," and "Ding Dong Daddy", and "Confessin'" and all those numbers. That was 19 --
Yeah, that was in Los Angeles.
'30. 1930. And from then on we just -- you just recorded and recorded, and did everything.
